newsitem.title: FRANCE: US asks allies to join big spyplane project-paper.
newsitem.headline: US asks allies to join big spyplane project-paper.

text.p: The United States has invited Britain, Germany and France to join it in a major project to develop a new unmanned spy plane, the French newspaper le Monde reported on Friday.

The respected Paris daily said Under-Secretary of Defence Paul Kaminski had asked Washington's European allies to hold a meeting in April on cooperation in the project, dubbed New Advanced Concept Technology Demonstration Initiative (ACTD).
The French Defence Ministry had no immediate comment on the report.

The United States currently has two such aircraft projects under way linked to ACTD and the meeting would explore whether London, Paris and Bonn wished to join -- and help finance -- them or other similar programmes to come.

The main project being developed is Teledyne Ryan's giant Global Hawk aircraft designed to fly at an altitude of 20,000 metres (over 60,000 ft) for up to 40 hours, sending back instant intelligence data. The prototype has a wingspan of 116 feet.
Washington wants up to 40 such planes, each costing about $33 million including its accompanying ground control station, Le Monde said.
The main advantage of such unmanned craft is that they could be directed to circle for long periods over trouble spots like North Korea or the Gulf without endangering flight crew.
The U.S. offer comes as France and Germany continue discussions over whether to press ahead with an existing European spy satellite programme independent of the United States.

French policy makers insist that plans for a common European defence policy, even in coordination with the United States, are doomed if Europe lacks its own space-based intelligence-gathering facilities.
